newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds range-bound, future uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds range-bound, future uncertain.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds ended flat after a rangebound day on Tuesday, taking their lead from listless German Bunds and slightly easier U.S. Treasuries, with all eyes on forthcoming U.S. data, traders said.
They said the underlying mood of the market remained positive, although caution was emerging and views were mixed on the curve.

"The U.S. is pulling prices down," one trader said. "Also Bunds are playing around 103. It is difficult to see where it is going. The fundamental trend is a bit bullish, but people are contemplating taking some profits."
"Curve wise people are looking at their options. Some are putting on flattening trades and others steepening trades. There is no consensus view," another trader said.

Traders said interest reemerged in the shorter maturity paper on Tuesday as well as in the five-to 10 year range. But it was at the expense of the very long-dated bonds where interest tailed off in comparison with last week.
They noted that money market rates, which have been rising strongly in recent days, paused for breath on Tuesday.
The one week repo rate was 4.07/14 percent against Monday's 4.05/15 percent.
Traders said there was little impact from the slight easing of liquidity as the Belgian Treasury took only 85 billion francs of T-bills against 128 billion coming to maturity.

They also noted that the immediate future would be heavily influenced by the flow of figures due from the United States this week -- particularly Friday including non-farm payrolls, personal spending, factory orders and the National Association of Purchasing Managers index.
Another influence would be new bond supply coming on stream.
"There was supply yesterday and more coming, so the market will tend to stay a bit soft," one trader said.
The yield of the benchmark 10-year OLO ended Tuesday at 5.63 percent against 5.65 percent late Monday, and the spread over Bunds edged out to 10 basis points from nine.
The front month futures contract was six basis points higher at 121.86.
